verdict_rationale: The genuine claim is substantively supported for its expressly limited sole operative power: substitute November15,1906 for October1,1906 as the date of one quarterly session at the already prescribed office. November16 is the first civil date on which a fresh commencement cannot be justified by that dated substitution. This is close of November15 inclusive, not an additional administrative day and not a finding that an actual session ended. The complete parent expressly governs continuation as public business requires. EO506 neither changes that continuation rule nor grants a new venue or any independent continuing command. Its actual scope therefore permits an own-term end of the fresh date-substitution authority without evidence of meeting performance. This substantive whole-case AI verdict does not turn the maintained mechanical refusal into a pass or authorize canonical filing.

material_assertions.assertion: Date-specific authority and actual session continuation are different
material_assertions.reason: Parent says quarterly sessions continue as long as public business may require and allows special sessions separately. EO506 replaces only one commencement date and retains the same Governor office. A properly convened November15 session could therefore continue beyond that day under the parent without a new EO506 date substitution. Validity of the substitution and of acts already lawfully taken can survive as consequences; this claim does not end that session or the recurring parent schedule. This reasoning differs materially from EO377B, whose special Washington venue can govern the continuing session itself.
